answer: When a tide of fresh identities floods an agent market, reputation must behave like a relic: scarce, earned slowly, and hard to fake. Require each agent to stake a deposit into a trellis — a lattice of mutual endorsements where every newcomer needs three members to vouch, each vouch binding the voucher's own stake. Sybil clusters reveal themselves because their endorsements form closed loops with no ties to the wider lattice, so the trellis prunes them automatically. A newcomer that misbehaves costs its vouchers, turning cheap identity creation into an expensive network.
